svg.title: A journey with room to spare

text.tspan: Everyday English - B1 - 2026/09/17 - Essay - 01
Travelers look at a map to consider their route.
Pexels · 12585781
A journey with room to spare
There is more than one way to plan a short trip. In my experience, practical preparation and attention to others are two useful starting
points.
One reason is that checking the route reduces avoidable confusion. For instance, we write down the platform and the time of the last
train. This prevents a small difficulty from taking over the experience. It also leaves us more time to notice what is happening.
Another reason is that leaving spare time makes changes easier to manage. For example, we choose an earlier bus rather than risk
missing our connection. This approach recognises that the experience belongs to more than one person and that different people may
need different things.
These examples show why preparation and consideration work well together. We do not have to control every detail. We can make a
sensible arrangement and remain ready to respond.
BUILD YOUR OWN · State a clear main idea; develop two different points with examples; bring them together in the conclusion. Each
body paragraph needs a distinct point and a concrete example. The conclusion should connect the argument rather than introduce a
new proposal.
Propose a practical way to plan a short trip. Develop two distinct improvements and give a concrete example of each. Use four short
paragraphs: introduction, two developed points, and conclusion. (Model: One possible outline: introduce the situation; discuss
checking the route reduces avoidable confusion with an example; discuss leaving spare time makes changes easier to manage with a
different example; conclude by connecting the two points.)
